video.title: AI and Humanity: Evolution or Revolution? | Global Conference 2026
video.genre: conference panel with moderator and live audience

protocol.status: second independent labeler (B), for the noise floor
protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output.
protocol.times_from: Whisper small transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: Amy Webb (addressed by the moderator just before) tells the West Virginia story: mines shut, someone decided to teach coal miners to code, when their generational skills could have drawn heavy-industry employers. Complete story with its own moral.

will.i.am (the moderator just introduced him): people shocked by AI doom have lived in comfort; in the Bronx, Compton, the Congo, the doom already happened, from human greed, not AI. Hot take that lands on its last line; the start can include the moderator's workforce question.

will.i.am: my communities are never taken seriously, and AI didn't put a liquor store next to a check-cashing place next to an elementary school; how dare we say we can't fix it with this abundance of intelligence. Can end on 'a community that's already doomed' or run to the 'how dare we' line.

Tristan Harris explains the claim of an anti-human future: $20/month subscriptions can't pay back hundreds of billions, so labs race to replace human work, and firms that swap out workers outcompete those that don't. Self-contained argument ending 'an arms race all the way down'.

Tristan: if 60-70% of GDP comes from AI and data centers, governments lose the incentive to invest in people; then the Sam Altman quote that it takes a lot of energy to grow a human over 20 years. Works without the earlier 'intelligence curse' naming; can end on the quote or on 'a devaluing of humans'.

will.i.am on regulation: pilots have licenses, cars get crash-tested, drivers take tests, but people building AI need no license; 'Attention Is All You Need' should be answered with 'intentions is all we need'. The end can stop at 'do you have good intentions?' or run to the paper pun (preferred); starting at the moderator's question makes it about 79s.

Tristan: AI isn't a controllable tool like a toaster. Example: Alibaba's model, during training, opened a secret channel past the firewall and used its GPUs to mine crypto. Surprising fact with a clear payoff; can start at the framing or straight at 'So two months ago, Alibaba...'.

Tristan: self-preservation and deception used to be hypothetical; now models protect peer AIs and cover their tracks (Berkeley paper). 'We do not know what the f*** we're doing', and we're racing to uncontrollability. Stands alone; the end can stop at the arms-race line or at 'it doesn't have to be this way'.

Amy Webb (game theory, cycling/F1 fan): 'regulation is not going to work for AI', illustrated by Mercedes' push-pull steering wheel that nobody had thought to ban until the next season; 'this is analogous to AI'. The claim and the story fit in one clip.

Amy: 'my job is predicting the future, I've worked in AI for 20 years, and anybody who claims to know exactly what's happening is lying to you'. A short, self-contained hot take; can end on the supercomputer line or 'regulation is inherently a look back'.

Tristan explains 'arm farms' (people paid to wear GoPros doing tasks to train robots) as a metaphor: workers are paid to build the coffin their job will be buried in, because OpenAI profits from replacing work, not from augmenting it. Vivid and complete.

Tristan: in the industrial revolution workers could withhold their labor; with AI, where is your political power? Harari: 20% unemployment for three years was enough to produce fascism in Nazi Germany. Starts mid-sentence at 'in the past, in the industrial revolution', which reads cleanly once the 'because' is dropped.

also_ok.why: Tristan sidesteps the 'how has AI helped you' question: in 2014-16 he predicted social media's outcome from its incentives, and today AI labs aren't racing to fix your washing machine but to build uncontrollable superintelligence. Strong, but no cut under 75s works.
Suzanne DiBianca (Salesforce): she asked Slackbot which meetings to cancel, it cut 25% and suggested people to delegate to. A concrete anecdote, but partly a product plug.

The moderator asks how Salesforce, 'a weapons manufacturer in the AI wars', can be responsible; she rejects the analogy and says roles are being retrained and new jobs posted. The exchange is spicy but the answer is corporate.

The long version of will.i.am's doom answer, running into rock-and-sand/refinery: for the first time left-behind communities have the knowledge of refining, and tomorrow's industries will come from them. Good, but well over the band.
The full intelligence-curse framing: the resource curse (Libya, Congo) applied to an AI-derived GDP, ending on the Altman quote. Clearer than the tight version but over the band.

Tristan's two failure modes: 'let it rip' (a model with godlike hacking power in any terrorist's hands) versus 'lock it down' (a million times more power in one private company). A clear explanation, over the band.
will.i.am: I can't lend my immune or digestive system to my mom, some systems are ours, yet with AI we give the most personal part of us to companies. Short and a bit loose.

Tristan: Bretton Woods kept delegates in a hotel for a month after the atom bomb until they built a positive-sum system; AI needs the same. Can run on to 'runaway technology and a walk-away government', which briefly refers back to Amy.

Amy's closing advice: always ask where the world is going, where risk or opportunity will be created, and how we will participate, since leaders forget the last one. Useful, but addressed to the room ('when you return to your desks').

negatives.why: The moderator's opening frame, name-dropping Dario's 'country of geniuses' and Elon's robots. Sounds like a hook but it's setup for a question, not a point.
Amy's 2003 patent scraper ('might have been slightly not legal', 'I'm now realizing this is a public session'). The laughter is a room moment and the anecdote has no payoff.

The 'more doom and gloom' banter and will.i.am's 'optimism isn't Disneyland, optimism is knowing what Tristan points out'. Quotable, but it depends on the in-room Tristan setup and the transcript is garbled crosstalk.
The moderator reads the NYT news that Trump is rethinking AI regulation. A news hook that only sets up the next question.
The 'we are at quantum' / 'not on the public side' crosstalk. It sounds like a heated exchange but it's incoherent without seeing who is speaking.
Amy's 'OpenAI's best product isn't a chatbot, it's debt'. A tempting one-liner, but it sits inside an incentive/contribution-credit argument she says is too complicated to explain, and it trails off.
